arxiv-2112-09469.title: Nuclear transparency of the charged hadron produced in the inclusive electronuclear reaction
arxiv-2112-09469.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by . The nuclear transparency of the charged hadron produced in the inclusive ( e , e ′ ) (e,e^{\prime}) reaction on the nucleus has been calculated using Glauber model for the nuclear reaction. The color transparency (CT) of the produced hadron and the short-range correlation (SRC) of the nucleons in the nucleus have been incorporated in the Glauber model to investigate their effects on the nuclear transparency of the hadron. The calculated nuclear transparencies for the proton and pion are compared with the data.

arxiv-2304-04551.title: Stability of relativistic tidal response against small potential modification
arxiv-2304-04551.creator: Takuya Katagiri, Hiroyuki Nakano, Kazuyuki Omukai
arxiv-2304-04551.description: Abstract The tidal response of compact objects in an inspiraling binary system is measured by a set of tidal Love and dissipation numbers imprinted in the gravitational waveforms. While a four-dimensional black hole in vacuum within General Relativity has vanishing Love numbers, a black hole in alternative theories of gravity can acquire non-vanishing Love numbers.

arxiv-2411-02804.title: Beyond the Traditional VIX: A Novel Approach to Identifying Uncertainty Shocks in Financial Markets
arxiv-2411-02804.creator: Ayush Jha *, Abootaleb Shirvani, Svetlozar T. Rachev, Frank J. Fabozzi
arxiv-2411-02804.description: Abstract We introduce a new identification strategy for uncertainty shocks to explain macroeconomic volatility in financial markets. The Chicago Board Options Exchange Volatility Index (VIX) measures market expectations of future volatility, but traditional methods based on second-moment shocks and time-varying volatility of the VIX often fail to capture the non-Gaussian, heavy-tailed nature of asset returns.

arxiv-2508-05110.title: Necessity of Block Designs for Optimal Locally Private Distribution Estimation Thanks: This work was supported by an Australian Government Research Training Program (RTP) Scholarship. Thanks: This is a preprint of a paper accepted for presentation at ITW 2025.
arxiv-2508-05110.creator: Abigail Gentle
arxiv-2508-05110.description: Abstract Local differential privacy represents the gold standard for preserving the privacy of data before it leaves the device, and distribution estimation under this model has been well studied. Recently, protocols built upon balanced incomplete block designs were shown to achieve optimal error for this problem. However, it remained unknown whether other constructions could also be optimal.

arxiv-2511-15997.title: Sensorium Arc: AI Agent System for Oceanic Data Exploration and Interactive Eco-Art
arxiv-2511-15997.creator: Noah Bissell, Ethan Paley, Joshua Harrison, Juliano Calil, Myungin Lee
arxiv-2511-15997.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Noah Bissell, Ethan Paley, Joshua Harrison, Juliano Calil, Myungin Lee. Sensorium Arc (AI reflects on climate) is a real-time multimodal interactive AI agent system that personifies the ocean as a poetic speaker and guides users through immersive explorations of complex marine data. Built on a modular multi-agent system and retrieval-augmented large language model (LLM) framework, Sensorium enables natural spoken conversations with AI agents that embodies the ocean’s perspective, generating responses that blend scientific insight with ecological poetics.

pmc-10627067.title: Toll-Like Receptor (TLR) 1, 2, and 6 Gene Polymorphisms Support Evidence of Innate Immune Factors in Schizophrenia
pmc-10627067.creator: Carlo E Sotelo-Ramírez, Beatriz Camarena, Marco Antonio Sanabrais-Jiménez, Julio Uriel Zaragoza-Hoyos, Bruno Ordoñez-Martínez, Raul I Escamilla-Orozco, Beatriz Gómez-González
pmc-10627067.description: IntroductionSchizophrenia is a complex psychiatric disorder with an important genetic contribution. Immunological abnormalities have been reported in schizophrenia. Toll-like receptor (TLR) genes play an important role in the activation of the innate immune response, which may help to explain the presence of inflammation in people with this disorder.

pmc-10735342.title: TRENDS IN SUPPORTS FOR FAMILY CAREGIVERS OF OLDER ADULTS THROUGH MEDICAID HOME AND COMMUNITY-BASED SERVICES IN THE US
pmc-10735342.creator: Katherine Miller, Elise Parrish, Johanna Thunell
pmc-10735342.description: The aging population in the United States, combined with the dominant preference of older adults to remain in the home and community, has increased the demand for unpaid (family) caregivers - a role often undertaken by spouses. Despite known adverse effects of caregiving on health and economic well-being, few systematic policies financially supporting caregivers exist.

pmc-11463231.title: Innovation in viruses: fitness valley crossing, neutral landscapes, or just duplications?
pmc-11463231.creator: Paul Banse, Santiago F Elena, Guillaume Beslon
pmc-11463231.description: Viruses evolve by periods of relative stasis interleaved with sudden, rapid series of mutation fixations, known as evolutionary bursts. These bursts can be triggered by external factors, such as environmental changes, antiviral therapies, or spill-overs from reservoirs into novel host species. However, it has also been suggested that bursts may result from the intrinsic evolutionary dynamics of viruses.

pmc-11464317.title: Early warning of Aspergillus contamination in maize by gas chromatography-ion mobility spectrometry
pmc-11464317.creator: Yucan Qin, Haoxin Lv, Yating Xiong, Lin Qi, Yanfei Li, Ying Xin, Yan Zhao
pmc-11464317.description: IntroductionAs one of the main grain crops in China, maize is highly susceptible to Aspergillus infection during processing, storage and transportation due to high moisture at harvest, which results in the loss of quality. The aim of this study is to explore the early warning marker molecules when Aspergillus infects maize kernels.

pmc-11522811.title: Focusing in on the Danon Disease Heart
pmc-11522811.creator: Charles A. Tharp, Matthew R.G. Taylor
pmc-11522811.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Panel-based genetic testing, where available, has advanced diagnostic speed and permits an understanding of genotype-phenotype relationships, prognostic considerations, and access to early but promising gene therapy trials (A Gene Therapy Study of RP-A501 in Male Patients With Danon Disease; NCT06092034).1 Although expansion of clinical testing is essential for improved diagnosis and management

pmc-12389664.title: Elastoplastic Modeling of Kevlar® Composite Laminates: A Cyclic Loading Approach for In-Plane Characterization
pmc-12389664.creator: Rene Alejandro Canceco de la Cruz, Luis Adrián Zúñiga Avilés, Gabriel Plascencia Barrera, Alberto Díaz Díaz, José Martin Herrera Ramírez
pmc-12389664.description: This study investigates the elastoplastic behavior of phenol formaldehyde/polyvinyl butyral matrix (70% PF/30% PVB) reinforced with Kevlar® fibers through comprehensive in-plane tensile testing. Cyclic loading–unloading tests were conducted at a 100%/min strain rate using a universal testing system at room temperature on 04, 904, and ±45s laminates.

pmc-12585666.title: Accelerating discovery and rational engineering of antibody modalities using Cryo- EM
pmc-12585666.creator: Tilak Gupta, Surajit Banerjee
pmc-12585666.description: As the need for novel therapeutic modalities is growing, researchers require innovative strategies and transformative technologies to overcome the limitations of traditional antibody discovery methodologies. Cryo-electron microscopy (Cryo-EM) has been successfully established as a powerful technique to accelerate antibody drug discovery processes.

pmc-12696164.title: Single-cell multi-omics for precision cardiovascular and longevity medicine: from methods to clinical translation
pmc-12696164.creator: Thiago Guimarães Osório, Estefania Pavesi, Khalil Abou El-Ardat, Needa Qureshi, Leanne Cassidy, Terrence Lee St. John, Nicole Sirotin, Bartlomiej Piechowski-Jozwiak
pmc-12696164.description: BackgroundSingle-cell multi-omics (SCMO) technologies simultaneously profile multiple molecular layers (e.g., DNA, RNA, proteins) within individual cells. Unlike traditional bulk analyses that average signals across thousands of cells, SCMO captures the unique molecular characteristics of each cell, potentially transforming our understanding of disease pathogenesis and clinical management.

pmc-13260304.title: Construction of chiral ZnO/BMP-2 dual functional coating on the surface of Ti implants for anti-infection and enhancement of osseointegration
pmc-13260304.creator: Yuan Fan, Haiyan Yao, Junchao Wei, Yipeng Hu
pmc-13260304.description: Titanium (Ti) implants are widely used in bone defect repair, however, postoperative infections and insufficient osseointegration would lead to implant failure. Therefore, it is much critical and necessary to construct antibacterial and osteogenic coatings on the surface of Ti implants to improve the successful rate of operation.

pmc-13643541.title: Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing
pmc-13643541.creator: Sebastian König, Kerstin Bode
pmc-13643541.description: Corresponding Author Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) has rapidly evolved from a niche physiological pacing technique into a cornerstone of contemporary cardiac pacing. Following accumulating observational evidence and recent consensus recommendations,1 LBBAP is increasingly being adopted for patients requiring high ventricular pacing burden because it preserves physiological ventricular activation while offering high implantation success and excellent long-term electrical performance.
